name: Hush
subtitle: part two: Thursday
story: On Thursday afternoon, as promised, her answer came across the valley. Half the town stood in the snow to hear it. It was yes. Then, a few seconds later and very faintly, a second word: 'obviously'. They are getting married in spring. The vows have to be shouted five days early to arrive on time.
hook: On Hush, walking is quicker than shouting.
cover: She got there before her answer did.
beats: Half the town came out to hear it.
It was yes. Then, a few seconds later, very faintly: 'obviously'.
odd_line: The wedding is in spring. The vows go out five days early.
rule: Wedding vows must be shouted at least five days in advance.
question: What would you shout across the valley?
extra: If you missed part one: on Hush, a shout takes five days to cross the valley.

beats.text:
A shout takes five days
to cross Hush.
Walking is quicker.

In March, he shouted
across the valley.
Would she marry him?

Seven months to decide.
Then five days was too long.

She got there Wednesday,
and said nothing.
You never spoil a shout.

I said I'd be there on Thursday.
Half the town came too.

episode.caption:
Part one is No. 003, a few posts down: in March he shouted a proposal across the valley, and her answer was due on Thursday.

She shouted her answer and set off straight after it. On Wednesday night she found him on the valley floor, where he'd been all week, and walked him home through snow up to her knees. They sat up by the stove and said nothing. You never spoil a shout.

On Thursday the bakery shut at three. Half the town stood on the valley floor with flasks, not talking, so as not to drown it out. At ten past four the snow stopped, as if it wanted to listen too.

Custom says you answer a shout with a shout, so he did, with her standing next to him. It reaches her empty house on Tuesday. I'm walking round to hear it, and I'll put what he said in the comments.

The wedding is in spring. The vows go out five days early.

What would you shout across the valley?
